name: Ruby interpreter
meaning: The runtime that executes Ruby source and provides Ruby language behavior.
context: Ruby language and standard-library semantics; language and explicitly available core-library semantics.

name: Ruby object
meaning: A Ruby value that has a class and can respond to methods.
context: Ruby language and standard-library semantics; language and explicitly available core-library semantics.

name: integer division
meaning: Division whose integer result follows the language’s integer rounding rule.
context: Ruby language and standard-library semantics; language and explicitly available core-library semantics.

name: Ruby truthiness
meaning: The condition rule under which only false and nil are false-like.
context: Ruby language and standard-library semantics; language and explicitly available core-library semantics.

name: string interpolation
meaning: Inserting an expression’s value into supported string syntax.
context: Ruby language and standard-library semantics; language and explicitly available core-library semantics.

name: object aliasing
meaning: Two or more references reaching the same object rather than independent copies.
context: Ruby language and standard-library semantics; language and explicitly available core-library semantics.

name: symbol
meaning: An immutable named Ruby value often used for identifiers or keys, distinct from a String.
context: Ruby language and standard-library semantics; language and explicitly available core-library semantics.

name: explicit fetch
meaning: Reading an entry with a deliberate missing-entry policy rather than silently assuming presence.
context: Ruby language and standard-library semantics; language and explicitly available core-library semantics.

name: hash default
meaning: A value or computation used for a missing key, which need not insert an entry.
context: Ruby language and standard-library semantics; language and explicitly available core-library semantics.

name: exclusive range
meaning: A range whose final endpoint is excluded from the represented interval.
context: Ruby language and standard-library semantics; language and explicitly available core-library semantics.

name: loop control
meaning: Explicitly skipping an iteration or leaving a loop rather than merely changing an output.
context: Ruby language and standard-library semantics; language and explicitly available core-library semantics.

name: case matching
meaning: Selecting a when branch using each pattern’s matching behavior rather than assuming universal equality.
context: Ruby language and standard-library semantics; language and explicitly available core-library semantics.

name: method-local scope
meaning: The local names belonging to a method body rather than automatically sharing an outer local scope.
context: Ruby language and standard-library semantics; language and explicitly available core-library semantics.

name: keyword argument
meaning: A method argument associated with a declared keyword name.
context: Ruby language and standard-library semantics; language and explicitly available core-library semantics.

name: double splat
meaning: Ruby syntax for gathering or expanding keyword arguments, distinct from positional splat handling.
context: Ruby language and standard-library semantics; language and explicitly available core-library semantics.

name: yield
meaning: Invoking the block supplied to the current Ruby method, with optional yielded arguments.
context: Ruby language and standard-library semantics; language and explicitly available core-library semantics.

name: block-local variable
meaning: A name explicitly limited to a block, which can shadow an outer local of the same name.
context: Ruby language and standard-library semantics; language and explicitly available core-library semantics.

name: lambda arity
meaning: The argument-count contract enforced by a Ruby lambda.
context: Ruby language and standard-library semantics; language and explicitly available core-library semantics.

name: captured binding
meaning: A surrounding variable binding retained by a closure rather than an automatically frozen snapshot of its earlier value.
context: Ruby language and standard-library semantics; language and explicitly available core-library semantics.

name: safe navigation
meaning: Calling a method unless its receiver is nil, without suppressing errors on other receivers.
context: Ruby language and standard-library semantics; language and explicitly available core-library semantics.
